definitions.explanation: A decorated miniature shrine carried on poles by a group of people during festivals. It is believed to house the spirit of a deity during the procession.

examples.japanese: {神輿|みこし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担|かつ}ぐ→担ぐ：03917_katsugu⟧。
⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{神輿|みこし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{通|とお}った→通る：01243_tooru⟧。
examples.english: A portable shrine passed through during the festival.

examples.japanese: ⟦{町内会|ちょうないかい}→町内会：10193_chounaikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦みんな→みんな：02972_minna⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{神輿|みこし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担|かつ}いで→担ぐ：03917_katsugu⟧⟦{練|ね}り{歩|ある}いた→練り歩く：13881_neriaruku⟧。
examples.english: Everyone in the neighborhood association carried the portable shrine in a parade through the streets.

notes:
USAGE:
The core verb collocation is {神輿|みこし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担|かつ}ぐ→担ぐ：03917_katsugu⟧ (to carry a mikoshi on one's shoulders). The figurative idiom {神輿|みこし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担|かつ}ぐ→担ぐ：03917_katsugu⟧ can also mean to put someone forward as a figurehead or leader.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Portable shrines are central to many Japanese festivals (⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧). Carriers shout わっしょい as they parade the shrine through the streets. The shrine temporarily houses the local deity ({氏神|うじがみ}) during the festival.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神輿|みこし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担|かつ}ぐ→担ぐ：03917_katsugu⟧: to carry a portable shrine
- {神輿|みこし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{練|ね}り{歩|ある}く→練り歩く：13881_neriaruku⟧: to parade the shrine through the streets
- {神輿|みこし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{上|あ}げる→上げる：02443_ageru⟧: to lift up the shrine
